key_insight: Structure-preserving, Fourier-based quantum circuits can accurately simulate wave-equation dynamics on a trapped-ion processor while extracting meaningful observables directly from samples.
engineering_relevance: The results show that near-term quantum hardware can represent and track structured PDE behavior over large encoded grids, making observable-first simulation a practical path for scalable quantum engineering workflows.
method: Encode 1D and 2D acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics with variable mass on Quantinuum H2-2.
Use structure-preserving Fourier-based circuits and product-formula evolution to maintain the physics of the dynamics.
Estimate subdomain kinetic energies from measurement samples instead of reconstructing full fields.
evidence_signal: Across all tested problems, H2-2 kinetic-energy trajectories matched classical dynamics with mean absolute errors between 5.9×10^-3 and 2.4×10^-2 on grids up to 1024 points and 32×32.
watch_item: Compiled circuit cost grows roughly quadratically with grid qubits, and for some models the cost also increases with the number of product-formula steps, which may limit scaling.
paper_title: Structure-Preserving Quantum Simulation of Wave Equations on a Trapped-Ion Processor
